name: Rustwater Layering Rig
description: A full-body survival stack built for the Shelf's acid-laced downpours. The outermost layer is a knee-length anorak cut from salvaged industrial tarp material — once corporate safety-orange, now faded to a streaky rust-and-cream, with mismatched patches of rubberized canvas heat-bonded over the shoulders and collar where the acid eats fastest. Underneath sits a dense thermal pullover in charcoal wool-synth blend, the left sleeve replaced entirely with a different fabric — darker, heavier, clearly scavenged from something else. Cargo trousers in faded olive feature six pockets, two of which are sealed with mismatched zippers, one with a strip of silver self-repair tape holding the seam together at the hip. The legs are tucked into calf-high boots with soles that have been rebuilt so many times the tread is a patchwork of different rubber compounds — black, grey, and one strip of deep red. A wide salvaged neoprene neck gaiter hangs loose around the throat, ready to pull up over the nose and mouth when rain hits. Fingerless gloves in cracked synthetic leather cover both hands, the right one reinforced across the knuckles with a strip of chrome salvage — a discarded aug-brace repurposed as protection. A battered wide-brim hat in waxed cotton, stained dark at the crown, completes the silhouette.
functionality: Acid-rain resistance via tarp anorak and rubberized shoulder patches. Thermal retention in the wool-synth underlayer. Six cargo pockets for tools, rations, and survival gear. Boot soles rebuilt for grip on wet industrial grating. Chrome knuckle brace doubles as impact protection. Gaiter provides respiratory filter layer in chemical environments.
what_it_says: This person has been on the Shelf long enough to know exactly what kills you — acid rain, cold, and exposure in that order. Every layer was chosen to solve a problem. Nothing is decorative. The mismatched repairs aren't shameful; they're a record of survival. The chrome knuckle piece says they've thought about close-quarters trouble too.
worn_by: people who've learned the hard way
manufacturer: Self-assembled from salvage and street-market components
price_range: Φ12–Φ40 (assembled over months from individual finds)
story_hooks: The chrome knuckle brace is actually a piece of a military-grade prosthetic arm — and its original owner may still be looking for it.
The acid-resistant tarp patches are cut from the same industrial lot used to seal a corporate dumping site — and they're faintly radioactive in a way the wearer doesn't yet know.
The self-repair tape is running out, and the hip seam is the only thing keeping a hidden interior pocket — and what's inside it — from falling into the street.

physical_description.visual_profile: A weathered, layered survival silhouette that reads as post-industrial scavenger. The figure appears bulky and utilitarian, with visible patching and material mismatches throughout. The overall impression is someone who has rebuilt themselves from salvage—nothing matches, everything works. The wide-brim hat and neck gaiter create a wrapped, fortress-like head profile.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately oversized and loose for movement and layering. The anorak drapes past the hips. The cargo trousers are relaxed through the thigh with tapered calf entry. The pullover sits slightly baggy to accommodate the thermal layer beneath. Everything is built for function over form—cinched where necessary, flowing where it matters for shelter.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged industrial tarp (anorak), wool-synth blend (pullover), heavy canvas patches, rubberized heat-bond repairs, faded cotton twill (trousers), neoprene (neck gaiter), cracked synthetic leather (gloves), waxed cotton (hat), multi-compound rubber (boot soles), chrome salvage metal (knuckle reinforcement)
physical_description.texture: Heavily textured and tactile. The anorak is stiff and weathered with visible heat-bonded seams. The wool-synth pullover is dense and nubbed. Patches show different fabric weaves—some smooth, some rough. The boots have a frankenstein quality with visible seam work. Chrome knuckles add metallic texture. Everything reads as touched by weather and repair.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant rust-orange faded to cream on the anorak with irregular grey and tan canvas patches. Charcoal wool pullover with darker (almost black) mismatched left sleeve. Faded olive trousers with silver tape accent at hip. Weathered waxed-tan hat with dark staining. Black, grey, and deep red rubber patchwork on boot soles. Chrome metal at knuckles catches light. Overall palette is desaturated earth tones punctuated by utilitarian greys and the occasional flash of salvaged metal.
physical_description.closures: Pragmatic mix: the anorak uses heavy friction-fit and implicit layering to seal. Trousers feature standard belt loops (likely with improvised cordage belt) and mixed zippers—two pockets sealed with mismatched salvage zippers, one hip seam held with self-repair tape instead of stitching. Boots lace-tied or friction-fitted. Gloves are loose fingerless pull-ons. Neck gaiter hangs free, meant to be pulled up on demand. Hat sits unadorned.
distinctive_features: Asymmetrical left sleeve replacement—visibly different fabric and darker tone
Heat-bonded canvas patches concentrated at shoulders and collar—areas of highest acid wear
Hip seam repaired with silver self-repair tape instead of traditional stitching
Right-hand knuckle guard made from salvaged chrome aug-brace
Boot soles rebuilt multiple times with visible patchwork of different rubber compounds
Mismatched zipper repairs on cargo pockets
Neoprene neck gaiter loose and ready-to-deploy
Waxed cotton hat with dark weathering stains at crown
No visible branding—purely functional salvage assembly
Faded safety-orange base color creating visual story of extended outdoor exposure
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 salvage. This is sub-grade territory—nothing here cost Φ in a store. Every component is scavenged, repaired, or jury-rigged. The multiple patches, mismatched materials, and chrome-knuckle reinforcement signal someone operating outside corporate supply chains.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this marks you as Shelf-side—the kind of person who lives in acid rain zones and has adapted rather than evacuated. It signals practical survivor culture, community salvage networks, and familiarity with environmental hazards corporate tiers don't face. This is the uniform of water-runners, waste-sorters, and the unregistered. Wearing it in a corpo zone would mark you immediately as sub-grade.
physical_description.condition_typical: Always broken-in and weathered. This garment never looks pristine—it's designed to look patched and repaired. The newer condition would be 'freshly salvaged with tape still crisp'; the worn condition is 'patches fading into the base material.' Acid staining, salt residue, and water rings are expected. Any pristine-looking component stands out as a recent find.
